newsitem.title: UK: BRITISH SOCCER CLUB BANS CELERY-THROWING FANS.
newsitem.headline: BRITISH SOCCER CLUB BANS CELERY-THROWING FANS.

text.p: A British soccer club has warned fans they will be banned for life if they bring celery into the stands.

Fans supporting Second Division club Gillingham are being frisked for celery after the club's hefty goalkeeper was pelted with the vegetable -- a vital visual component of a bawdy song popular on British football terraces for several years.
After issuing the crunch warning to fans, club safety officer Ken Tappenden told BBC Radio on Wednesday: "There is a safety implication here with the bringing of celery into the ground.
"We had incidents over a number of matches. They sang the song and then threw it up in the air. We estimate there must have been boxes of it in the air."
Goalkeeper Jim Stannard told the Daily Star tabloid: "Fat chance of me going on a diet. I like my pasta too much. Perhaps if they threw lasagne, I might take more notice."
